bull.b: Sustained comparable-sales and traffic growth indicates that Chili’s is gaining guest demand through stronger food, value, service, and marketing. This durable brand momentum can support higher restaurant productivity, improve operating leverage, and provide a foundation for continued growth over the next several quarters.

Significantly stronger operating and free cash flow improves Brinker’s ability to fund restaurant investments, remodels, debt reduction, and shareholder returns internally. Cash flow also exceeded accounting earnings in 2025–2026, supporting the quality and durability of the recent earnings recovery.

bull.t: Long-term unit and revenue growth plan
bull.b: The multi-year plan gives Brinker a visible path to expand beyond same-store sales through new units and larger trade areas. Combining unit growth with continued Chili’s momentum could broaden the revenue base, reinforce brand presence, and support sustained earnings growth through fiscal 2029.

bear.b: Although equity has recovered from prior negative levels, Brinker remains highly leveraged relative to its equity base. This reduces financial flexibility and leaves more cash flow exposed to interest costs, refinancing needs, or weaker restaurant performance if operating conditions soften.

Maggiano’s underperformance shows that the company’s recovery is uneven across brands and that the turnaround is taking longer than planned. Flat expected revenue and profit limit its contribution to consolidated growth, while continued traffic weakness could require additional management attention and investment.

Restaurant profitability remains sensitive to commodity, wage, occupancy, insurance, and marketing costs. Even with sales growth, these pressures can absorb operating leverage and constrain margin expansion, as reflected in management’s conservative 20–40 basis-point restaurant-margin improvement outlook for fiscal 2027.
